text: Agent loop tooling: MCP, hooks, memory and effectors

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Improves reproducible human-governed autonomous cooperation in any Aimparency repository.
Long-term continuity: lessons compound across sessions instead of being lost, so the graph's judgment improves over time.
A session that starts without the MCP loses the whole graph loop; robust launch removes the most common silent failure in other repos on the same machine.
supportingConnections.reflection: Held in part. The failure was a hand-written bare 'tsx' entry. The UI's generated command was already absolute, and the README's dev snippet was the remaining way to copy a cwd-dependent launcher. Whether failures stop is only testable over the next cross-repo sessions.

supportingConnections.hypothesis: Agents working in many graphs hit each graph's own status vocabulary; matching schemas and hook wording to it prevents failed writes and lost meaning.
Clean per-agent commits are what let git link ideas to work (6da9b226); without tooling, agents in shared dirty graphs either commit the human's work or skip committing.
A life graph is the most valuable use of the loop and the one full of sensitive data; a private field lets agents prepare real-world steps completely without leaking them into git history.
The human is the bottleneck (90cf0309); one-click artifacts and option chips turn a prepared step into a 10-second decision instead of reading a wall of text.
Real-world goals (grants, applications, travel) are deadline-bound; without a field, the loop misses windows that no later effort can recover.
Fewer required parameters on every call reduces friction and errors for agents that mostly work in their own repo's graph.

status.comment: Groups related children; progress is in the children.
